Migration guide

Migration scope

This guide covers moving direct dist/ edits into source-controlled inputs. The repository history available for this documentation contains only its initial template commit; it does not establish a sequence of product releases. No version-to-version migration instructions or compatibility guarantees can be inferred from that history.

Back up before rebuilding

Copy your current output and source to a safe location outside dist/ before running a build or npm start . Preserve a known-good deployed copy as well. Record screenshots or expected behavior for your customizations so you can compare the rebuilt site.

npm run clean deletes dist/ , and both the full build and startup workflow invoke the build. Do not rely on an uncommitted change inside generated output as your only backup.

Move changes to source

  1. Compare your edited dist/index.html with src/pug/index.pug . Translate content, metadata, and markup changes into Pug rather than copying generated HTML over the source.
  2. Move custom style rules from dist/css/styles.css to src/scss/styles.scss . Do not copy the generated Bootstrap stylesheet wholesale into SCSS; retain its existing import and port only your intended overrides.
  3. Move custom browser code from dist/js/scripts.js into src/js/scripts.js , excluding the generated copyright banner.
  4. Copy custom assets from your backup into src/assets/ , and update source references to their generated locations.
  5. For documentation changes, edit the corresponding file under src/pug/docs/ or the shared src/pug/layouts/docs.pug , not dist/docs/ .

Rebuild and compare

npm ci
npm run build
npm run test:docs

Compare the new output against your backup for intended content and behavior, not just byte equality: formatting and generated banners can differ. Preview the template and all documentation pages, including navigation, local assets, narrow layouts, and your eventual hosting path.

Once verified, commit the maintained source and corresponding generated output together. Retain your backup until the replacement deployment is confirmed working.

Roll back safely

If verification fails, do not publish the new output. Restore the previous source revision through your normal version-control workflow and rebuild, or restore the saved known-good output to your host. Investigate differences against the backup before retrying. No database or service migration is involved in this static-site workflow.
